snippet.title: Moses Moody Was ON FIRE In New Orleans!
snippet.description:
The Warriors won their third straight game, defeating the Pelicans 124–106. Golden State improves to 9–6, while New Orleans drops to 2–11.

Moses Moody delivered a breakout performance with 32 points and eight made threes, both career-highs. He also joined Stephen Curry and Klay Thompson as the only Warriors ever to hit at least seven threes in a single quarter, accomplishing the feat in the first quarter. Brandin Podziemski added 19 points, 3 rebounds, and 3 assists, while Stephen Curry contributed 9 points, 5 rebounds, and 3 assists.

Buddy Hield also made history, moving into 15th place on the all-time three-pointers made list, passing Paul Pierce as Golden State’s long-range shooting was dominant, knocking down 24 three-pointers in the game.

Trey Murphy III led the Pelicans with 20 points, 8 rebounds, and 4 steals.

snippet.title: NETS at WIZARDS | FULL GAME HIGHLIGHTS | November 16, 2025
snippet.description:
The Nets defeated the Wizards 129–106, improving to 2–11 on the season, while Washington falls to 1–12.

Michael Porter Jr. led the Nets with 34 points, shooting 11–18 from the field, while adding 9 rebounds and 7 assists. Notably, he has now recorded back-to-back games with 7 assists after never having a 7-assist game in his career prior. Tyrese Martin added 20 points, 4 assists, and three made threes off strong offensive play.

Brooklyn’s bench played a major role, outscoring Washington’s unit 51–31.

Kyshawn George paced the Wizards with 29 points, 6 rebounds, and 5 assists, while CJ McCollum contributed 17 points, including three three-pointers, along with 3 assists.

snippet.title: CLIPPERS at CELTICS | FULL GAME HIGHLIGHTS | November 16, 2025
snippet.description:
The Celtics defeated the LA Clippers 121–118. Boston led by as many as 24, and despite a late surge from the Clippers, the Celtics held on to move to 7–7 on the season. The Clippers drop to 4–9 with the loss.

Jaylen Brown led the way with 33 points, 13 rebounds, 3 assists, and 2 steals. Payton Pritchard knocked down eight threes, finishing with 30 points and 3 rebounds. Derrick White added 22 points, 7 rebounds, and 9 assists. Boston also capitalized on LA’s mistakes, turning 14 Clippers turnovers into 27 points, outscoring them 27–10 in that category.

James Harden delivered a huge performance with 37 points, 7 rebounds, 8 assists, and five threes. He erupted for 32 points in the second half, becoming just the fourth player this season to score 32+ in any half, joining Nikola Jokić, Jamal Murray, and Luka Dončić. Harden also poured in 18 points in the fourth quarter, shooting 5–8 from the field and 3–4 from three. John Collins added 17 points and 2 rebounds, while Ivica Zubac posted 16 points and 12 rebounds.
H
arden’s Back-to-Back Milestone:

Friday vs. Dallas: 41 PTS | 14 REB | 11 AST
Tonight vs. Boston: 37 PTS | 7 REB | 8 AST

With these performances, he becomes just the fourth player ever age 36 or older to record back-to-back 35/5/5 games, joining Stephen Curry, LeBron James (5×), and Kevin Durant (2×) — all active players.
